_what: THE WORKLOAD — what a week actually looks like on an agent/AI-automation role, written as ASSIGNMENTS the learner does for real. Not a syllabus: a ticket queue.
_why_this_file: Jordan, 2026-10-28: 'What would be work assignments that I would get from work? What does the actual workload look like? I know that you say it's exactly what we do, but we're on Telegram. What would they want professionally?' A course built from a job description teaches the description. A course built from the WORK teaches the job. This is the work.
_source_of_truth: Ticket shapes derived from the measured track (98-posting sample) plus the hiring-signal patterns those samples named: evaluation, observability, retrieval, tool calling, multi-agent, guardrails. Every assignment below carries the market term it trains.
_rule: An assignment is not complete until its artifact exists somewhere a stranger can open. This is the same rule as the engine's milestone gate — no artifact, no close.
label: The Workload — a week on the job

week.ticket: OPS-114: 'Our agent keeps failing overnight and nobody knows why.'
what_you_actually_do: Read the logs of a real scheduled run and find the last good and first bad execution.
Add structured logging to the failing path: run id, model, tokens, latency, error class.
Build one page that answers 'what failed in the last 24h and how often'.
Write the incident note: what broke, what you measured, what you changed.
week.artifact: a dashboard/chart URL or a committed log + the incident note
week.why_the_market_wants_it: Postings name observability in 40% of samples, and 'how do you debug a non-deterministic failure' is a standard interview question.
week.jordan_has: cron health standards, alarm debouncing, receipted logs — this is naming + one chart away

week.ticket: EVAL-7: 'Before we change the prompt, prove the change does not make it worse.'
what_you_actually_do: Build a small golden set: 10 real inputs with the output you consider correct.
Write a grader that scores an output against each case — exact, rubric, or model-graded.
Run it before and after a prompt change and report the delta with counts, not percentages of a tiny n.
Decide: ship or revert, and say which and why.
week.artifact: eval harness in a repo + a before/after table with n= stated
week.why_the_market_wants_it: The single most-named requirement in the sample. It is also the hardest to fake, which is why it separates candidates.
week.jordan_has: edu-extract.py IS this — model proposes, verifier deletes unverifiable output, with real rejection counts. Needs its rubric written down and its numbers published.

week.theme: Tool calling and a failure path
week.ticket: TOOL-42: 'The agent calls the pricing tool and sometimes passes a string where a number belongs.'
what_you_actually_do: Define the tool schema strictly (types, enums, required fields).
Make the tool reject bad input with a message the MODEL can act on.
Give the agent one retry with the error text, then fail closed.
Log the failure class so day 1's dashboard counts it.
week.artifact: a tool with schema validation + a test showing the bad-input path, and the retry counted
week.why_the_market_wants_it: Tool calling is the mechanism; guardrails are the trust story. Both appear in a quarter of postings each.

week.ticket: RAG-9: 'The assistant answers from last year's docs. Make it answer from the current ones.'
what_you_actually_do: chunk the 204K-token textbook TWO ways: fixed-size and structure-aware
embed locally with bge-small; store a vector index
answer 10 questions with citations back to chunk ids
measure hit@3, hit@5 and MRR on a hand-built question set, for BOTH chunkings
write one paragraph defending the chunk size from the numbers
week.artifact: retrieval service + hit@k for both chunkings + the chunking rationale with numbers
week.why_the_market_wants_it: RAG is in a third of postings and is the standard interview topic that reveals whether someone has shipped.
week.jordan_has: the phrase packs (25 Nepali phrases, sourced) — a real corpus to retrieve over
week._rescope: v1 assumed an embedding endpoint. MEASURED: no embedding model on either rail (30 and 47 models, zero embedding). Re-scoped to bge-small (~160MB, CPU) — real retrieval, small model, both stated.

week.theme: Multi-agent orchestration, and handing it over
week.ticket: ORCH-3: 'Split the job so a researcher agent and a writer agent do not block each other.'
what_you_actually_do: Draw the graph: nodes, state, the termination condition.
Implement it in LangGraph (or LangChain) with explicit state.
Prove a failure in one node recovers rather than hangs.
Write the handover: what a colleague needs to run it without you.
week.artifact: the graph in a repo + a state dump showing a recoverable failure + a README a stranger can follow
week.why_the_market_wants_it: The modal job names two frameworks. The handover README is the difference between 'built a demo' and 'owns a system'.

the_week_in_one_line: Find what broke, prove whether the fix helped, make the tool refuse bad input, answer from current documents, and hand the system to someone else.
_what_this_is_not: Not a tutorial series. Each ticket is the SHAPE of real work; the artifact is what closes it. Hours vary — day 2 and day 5 are the expensive ones.

_interview_mapping._note: Every ticket maps to a question the sample's interviewers ask. That is why the workload is the curriculum.

OPS-114.finding: All three failures are monitors exiting nonzero to REPORT, not crashes. status:failed cannot distinguish a broken job from an alerting one. DR gate has failed 3/3 with delivery_outcome=not_configured — a failing alarm nobody hears.
OPS-114.closed_because: dashboard built + rendered + read back in a browser; incident note written; three failures diagnosed to root cause

EVAL-7.golden_set: data/eval/golden-extract-ne.json (127 pairs, hand-reviewed, UBC open textbook)
EVAL-7.verdict: B better by 21 correct pairs. Pre-registered rule said KEEP A because fabricated went 0->1; the rule under-modelled the verbatim-src verifier, which deletes unverifiable units. Flagged to Jordan rather than silently re-graded.
EVAL-7.landed: edu-extract.py now has --prompt {a,b} defaulting to a; default model changed to kimi-k2.7-code because the old default was HTTP 410 ModelDeprecated/403.
EVAL-7.closed_because: golden set built+reviewed, grader selftested 5/5, 20 model calls run, decision rule evaluated, wiring proven end-to-end on the real EPUB

TOOL-42.finding: The ticket's bug did not reproduce naturally in 3 calls; it reproduced only when forced. The guard's value is as a BOUNDARY, not a fix for an observed rate. 3 calls cannot bound a rate.
own_defects_fixed: selftest polluted the production log (6 counted vs 2 real)
TOOL-42.closed_because: six bad-input classes rejected, rejection text proven actionable by a live model, fail-closed proven, log verified by reading it, 11/11 selftest

RAG-9.environment: CPU-only venv · fastembed 0.9.1 + onnxruntime 1.31.1 · no GPU, no embedding API

measured.english_only_on_nepali: 0/8, MRR 0.000 — never ranked a correct chunk in the top 10

RAG-9.finding: Retrieval WORKS on English (9/12) and FAILS on Nepali (2/8 best). Model language must match query language. My first run used only English questions and nearly reported a biased result as the answer.
RAG-9.chunking_answer: structural 1200-2600 split on section boundaries — the only config non-zero in BOTH languages
RAG-9.next: bigger multilingual model (e5-large / bge-m3, 2.2GB+) = Forge task; and BM25 hybrid, untested and likely strong on Devanagari
RAG-9.closed_because: chunked, embedded, searched, hit@k measured across 2 models x 2 chunkings x 2 query languages, chunk size defended from the numbers
